notes:
This was a resume run. Neither owned file existed yet: there was no partial work and no scratch files to clean up, and I created none. The two files are now written.

src/atlas/entries/rhythm.ts: 33 entries, every finding in the rhythm category.
src/atlas/entries/conduction.ts: 19 entries, every finding in the conduction category.

Each file exports only `entries`. Each also has a non-exported local reference table `R` for full references that are not yet in refs.ts. Each entry follows the schema and has:
- a one-line definition;
- 2–6 key features in reading order;
- criteria with short-form sources, each resolving to a full reference in the entry's sources;
- a mechanism of exactly two sentences in each language;
- at least two mimics, each with one discriminating feature and the leads to compare;
- pitfalls and PLAN §3 lesson ids;
- aka search keys (older names such as PSVT, LGL, sick sinus and hemiblock appear only here, never in prose);
- exemplar preferences, using the scenario ids planned in DECISION §9.

All criteria values use the 'current value' column of docs/curriculum/criteria.md, checked against these guidelines: Kusumoto 2018, Surawicz 2009, ESC SVT 2019, ESC VA/SCD 2022, ESC AF 2024, ESC pacing 2021, Drew 2010 and Sharma 2017.

Modern framing in the entries:
- 2:1 AV block is its own category. It cannot be typed as Mobitz I or II from the 2:1 segment; the entry gives nodal vs infranodal clues.
- High-grade AV block means two or more consecutive blocked P waves; ratios are written P:QRS.
- Mobitz I's key sign is a shorter PR after the pause. Mobitz II is a pacing indication even without symptoms.
- LBBB gives the AHA 2009 criteria and the strict Strauss criteria side by side. It also says the axis is not a criterion and gives the Sgarbossa/Smith rules (ST/S ≤ −0.25).
- Fascicular blocks use 'fascicular block' (never 'hemiblock'). The LAFB rules are −45° to −90°, qR in aVL and R-wave peak time ≥ 45 ms. LPFB is a diagnosis of exclusion.
- Trifascicular block means alternating BBB. Bifascicular block with a long PR is reported by its components.
- An rSr′ with QRS < 110 ms is a normal variant, not incomplete RBBB.
- SVT names follow the mechanism (AVNRT, AVRT, focal AT, flutter), with the RP′ 90 ms cut-off and the narrow-QRS approach. 'Junctional' is used, never 'nodal'.
- A wide-QRS tachycardia is treated as VT until proven otherwise: Brugada 1991, Vereckei aVR, Pava lead II and Wellens morphology criteria; no verapamil.
- Ectopy is described by NSVT, PVC burden (≥ 10 %) and coupling interval < 300 ms instead of Lown grades or 'triplets'.
- AIVR is not a marker of reperfusion.
- WPW: no reading of Q waves, LVH, BBB, axis or QT on pre-excited beats; no AV-nodal blockers in pre-excited AF.
- A short PR is enhanced AV-nodal conduction, not 'LGL'.

Every critical finding has an urgency statement: ventricular-escape-rhythm, vt-monomorphic, vt-polymorphic, torsades, ventricular-flutter, ventricular-fibrillation, asystole, av-block-2-mobitz2, av-block-high-grade, av-block-3. I also added urgency to time-sensitive major findings, including AF, SVT, 2:1 block, LBBB, WPW, bifascicular and trifascicular block, sinus pause and sinus node dysfunction.

Spanish uses Spain terms: derivación, aurícula, bloqueo de rama, bloqueo fascicular, TRIN/TRAV, RIVA, decimal commas. Chinese uses standard textbook terms.

The entries do not import anything from src/lab. FindingPage already shows the Heart Lab card through labHref(id). Many of these findings have lab scenarios (sinus rhythms, PAC, PVC, AF, flutter, AVNRT/SVT, junctional escape, VT, torsades, VF, AV blocks, RBBB/LBBB, LAFB/LPFB, WPW), so the link appears with no code change.
